rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Plasma lipoprotein remodeling and lipid absorption' in scope of plasma lipid metabolism; renamed to reflect the hepatic secretion/export processes distinguishing it from remodeling and absorption.

name: Lymphocyte cytotoxicity and antigen-driven activation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; specifically covers cytotoxic and antigen-driven lymphocyte activation, unlike T cell activation/differentiation or lymphocyte effector regulation siblings.

name: Nucleotide degradation and salvage
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Nucleotide, nucleoside and analogue metabolism'; narrowed to the degradation/salvage pathways distinct from that broader nucleoside/analogue focus.

name: Actin-driven cell shape remodeling
rationale: Overlapped with parent 'Neurite and cell shape morphogenesis' and sibling 'Neuronal projection outgrowth and regeneration'; narrowed to actin/cytoskeleton-based shaping distinct from projection outgrowth.

name: Chromatin and epigenetic regulation
rationale: Distinct from parent and siblings; siblings focus on genome stability, p53-driven responses, and protein stability, while this theme uniquely covers chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms.

name: Aldosterone-mediated sodium and water regulation
rationale: Too similar to parent 'fluid balance'; narrowed to the specific hormone-driven ion/water mechanism, distinguishing it from the angiotensin signalling sibling.

name: Muscle contraction and potassium homeostasis
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Muscle contraction and calcium homeostasis'; needs to specify the distinct ion focus of this theme.

name: DNA damage repair
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and though similar in theme to the parent, it does not literally repeat it; insufficient information to narrow further without overstepping.

name: Intrinsic apoptotic signalling
rationale: Collided with parents 'Mitochondrial apoptosis and its regulation'/'Apoptotic signalling'; renamed to contrast with sibling 'Extrinsic apoptotic signalling' and clarify pathway type rather than location.

name: Transendothelial leukocyte migration
rationale: Overlapped with sibling 'Chemokine-driven leukocyte chemotaxis'; renamed to specify the adhesion/transmigration step distinct from chemokine-gradient sensing.

name: p53-driven senescence and apoptotic pathways
rationale: Overlaps significantly with sibling 'p53-driven DNA damage response and cell cycle control'; sharpened to focus specifically on senescence and apoptosis outcomes rather than the broader DNA damage response, distinguishing it clearly.

name: Extracellular matrix glycosaminoglycan metabolism
rationale: Nearly repeated the parent name; specifying glycosaminoglycan/ECM matrix components distinguishes it from the parent and from the transport-focused sibling.

name: Phosphate group transport and metabolism
rationale: Too similar to sibling 'Nucleotide metabolism and transport'; narrowed to emphasize phosphate-specific handling that distinguishes this theme.

name: Mitotic division and cytokinesis
rationale: Distinct from parent (chromosome segregation) and sibling (segregation fidelity); this theme covers division/cytokinesis machinery, not segregation.

name: Neuronal development and synaptic transmission
rationale: No parent to repeat, and no sibling covers neuronal development plus synaptic transmission specifically; remains distinct.

name: Mitochondrial gene expression and protein complex assembly
rationale: No siblings and distinct from parent; name already specific to mitochondrial gene expression and complex assembly rather than RNA processing crosstalk.

name: Antimicrobial peptide defence
rationale: Distinct from parents (metal sequestration and general humoral effectors framing) and sibling (complement activation); already specific to antimicrobial peptides.

name: Virus-host interactions
rationale: Both children plus all members concern host factors and defences governing viral entry, replication, and innate sensing across the viral life cycle.

name: HDL metabolism and cellular cholesterol efflux
rationale: Distinct from parent (broader transport regulation) and sibling (homeostasis focus); this theme specifically covers HDL metabolism and efflux mechanisms.

name: Glycosaminoglycan and glycoprotein metabolism
rationale: No siblings to conflict with, and though related to the parent, it addresses metabolism broadly rather than repeating the parent's disorder focus.

name: Proteostasis and protein degradation
rationale: Both children and the direct members (ubiquitination signalling, ubiquitin-independent proteasomal degradation, stress granule disassembly) converge on maintaining protein homeostasis through degradation or clearance machinery, broader than either child alone but excluding unrelated processes like transcription or metabolism.

name: Neuronal morphogenesis in synapse maturation
rationale: Repeated parent's 'synapse formation and structural maturation' scope without adding specificity; renamed to emphasize morphogenetic processes within that maturation context.

name: Ciliary regulation of embryonic patterning
rationale: No parent to collide with, and distinct from siblings like Hedgehog signalling in neural tube patterning and Embryonic axial patterning and organogenesis by its specific focus on ciliary mechanisms in patterning.

name: Addictive substance response circuitry
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from both parents, adding specificity about addictive substances rather than repeating either parent term.

name: Vascular remodeling in wound healing
rationale: Repeated parent's scope without linking to fibroproliferative wound healing context; new name specifies vascular changes as part of that process.

name: Vesicle fusion and neurotransmitter exocytosis
rationale: Overlapped heavily with parent 'Neurotransmitter release and receptor signalling' and sibling 'Synaptic transmission and plasticity'; narrowed to the specific mechanism of vesicle fusion/exocytosis distinguishing it from both.

name: Digestive nutrient uptake and sugar transport
rationale: Name is distinct from parent and siblings; specifically addresses digestive nutrient uptake and sugar transport, not overlapping with others.

name: Protein glycosylation and glycosylation disorders
rationale: Union covers general protein glycosylation, dystroglycan/glycosylation-linked disorders, and O-glycosylation of TSR domain proteins, all being forms or defects of protein glycosylation.

name: Vascular smooth muscle phenotype switching
rationale: Name overlapped conceptually with parent 'ECM remodelling in vessels' scope; narrowed to specify vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype switching, distinguishing from endothelial-focused siblings.

name: Epithelial architecture and homeostasis
rationale: Covers adhesion/junctional biology, keratinized epidermal differentiation, and stem-cell renewal of intestinal epithelium, all being aspects of how epithelial tissues are organized and maintained; broader terms like 'adhesion' alone would exclude keratinization and stem cell homeostasis.

name: Nucleotide excision repair and UV response
rationale: Repeated the parent 'DNA damage repair'; specifying UV-induced photoproduct repair via nucleotide excision distinguishes it from base excision repair and oxidative damage response sibling.

name: Interferon-gamma and cytoplasmic innate antiviral responses
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is more specific than the parent by specifying interferon-gamma and cytoplasmic sensing mechanisms.

name: Mitochondrial proteostasis and biogenesis
rationale: Nearly identical to parent 'Mitochondrial dynamics and quality control' and sibling 'Mitochondrial organelle dynamics and quality control'; renamed to reflect distinct focus on protein quality and biogenesis rather than fission/fusion dynamics.

name: Cellular osmotic and salt stress response
rationale: Distinct from parent (vasopressin-mediated water reabsorption) and sibling (body fluid homeostasis); focuses on cellular-level osmotic/salt stress response mechanisms rather than systemic water balance.

name: Mechanotransduction in hair cells and muscle
rationale: Distinct from parent and sibling; specifies mechanotransduction in hair cells and muscle rather than general sensory/chemosensory transduction or detection.

name: rRNA and tRNA processing and modification
rationale: No siblings to collide with, and the name is distinct from the parent, which covers snRNA/snoRNA processing rather than rRNA and tRNA.

name: HIF-mediated hypoxia response
rationale: No siblings present and name is more specific than both parents, distinguishing the HIF-mediated mechanism from the broader stress/hypoxia themes.
